rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Lateral Shift and other topics  ·  Key Formula 5: Important relation in Lateral Shift  ·  ❌ Lateral shift depends on the refractive index of the slab material only. ✅ Lateral shift depends on ALL THREE: thickness $t$, angle of incidence $i$, AND refractive index $n$ (through the refraction angle $r$).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ At normal incidence, there is a lateral shift. ✅ At normal incidence ($i = 0°$), the lateral shift is ZERO. The ray passes straight through without any displacement.  ·  ❌ The lateral shift formula $d = t\sin(i-r)/\cos r$ works for prisms. ✅ This formula is ONLY for parallel-sided slabs. Prisms have non-parallel faces, so the emergent ray is deviated, not just shifted.  ·  ❌ A thicker slab always produces a proportionally larger shift for the same angle. ✅ Yes, the shift IS directly proportional to thickness: $d \propto t$. But the proportionality constant depends on $i$ and $n$.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The lateral shift is the same as the deviation angle. ✅ Lateral shift is a DISTANCE (measured in cm or m). Deviation angle is an ANGLE (measured in degrees). They are completely different quantities.  ·  ❌ Light passing through a glass slab changes its frequency. ✅ The frequency of light does NOT change when it passes through any medium. Only the speed and wavelength change: $v = c/n$ and $\lambda = \lambda_0/n$.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Lateral Shift
